E1.evidence: Maintainer-filed issue: "there are a lot of compile warnings for `using deprecated function`, we should try to upgrade/move away from these moving forward" -- https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/issues/152; a contributor names the functions: "They were `avcodec_register_all`, `avpicture_alloc`, and other `av`-related warnings." -- https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/pull/170

E2.evidence: usb_cam (ROS 2 driver node package) links FFmpeg's libavcodec/libswscale (CMakeLists: "pkg_check_modules(avcodec libavcodec REQUIRED)", "pkg_check_modules(swscale libswscale REQUIRED)"; package.xml "<depend>ffmpeg</depend>"). The warnings come from FFmpeg declarations marked deprecated that usb_cam still calls: at usb_cam 90d4d59e, src/usb_cam.cpp calls "avcodec_register_all();", "avpicture_alloc(", "avpicture_get_size(", "avpicture_layout(" and "avcodec_decode_video2("; FFmpeg n4.2 libavcodec/avcodec.h marks each of these attribute_deprecated, while n2.8 marks none. The resolving change (PR #207) replaces the calls in usb_cam's code, not the build system.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: FFmpeg (provider) at a release that deprecates functions usb_cam's code was written against; the issue asks to "upgrade/move away from these moving forward, while maybe keeping some around for backward compatibility".

E4.evidence: Compile warnings "using deprecated function" documented (issue) and attributed to "`avcodec_register_all`, `avpicture_alloc`, and other `av`-related warnings" (PR #170); the package still builds and runs.

units.name: usb_cam

units.name: FFmpeg
units.revision_basis: No source names the FFmpeg version. The ros2 branch at the time targeted ROS 2 Foxy/Galactic on Ubuntu 20.04 (PR #170's build log, same period, shows "/opt/ros/galactic/include/rclcpp"), whose ffmpeg packages are from the 4.2 series; all five deprecated calls carry attribute_deprecated in n4.2 and n4.2.4. Branch release/4.2 is used as a series-level label; unchanged by the resolution.

loudness_evidence: Compiler diagnostics at build: "there are a lot of compile warnings for `using deprecated function`" -- https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/issues/152; PR #170 had to suppress them to get a clean build: "add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wno-overflow -Wno-deprecated-declarations -Wno-switch)" -- https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/pull/170

resolution.summary: usb_cam PR #207 (ros2 branch) stops calling the deprecated FFmpeg functions on the libavcodec>52/>=55 code paths: removes "avcodec_register_all();", replaces avpicture_alloc with av_image_alloc, avpicture_get_size with av_image_get_buffer_size, avpicture_layout with av_image_copy_to_buffer, and drops av_init_packet/avcodec_decode_video2; the deprecated calls remain only inside #if LIBAVCODEC_VERSION_MAJOR < 55 / <= 52 branches.
resolution.evidence: Diff of https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/pull/207 (merge 77a774f5, 2022-11-23); no source shows a warning-free build of this revision against an identified FFmpeg revision. The issue was closed 2023-04-09 with "Closing" after a maintainer noted "#197 is already merged, cleansing started" (PR #197 targets the ROS 1 'develop' branch).

notes: consumer_built_against is inferred: n2.8 is the last FFmpeg release in which none of usb_cam's calls is marked attribute_deprecated (n3.0 deprecates avpicture_alloc/avpicture_get_size/avpicture_layout, n3.1 avcodec_decode_video2, n4.0 avcodec_register_all); usb_cam's FFmpeg code predates the ROS 2 port (ROS 1 PR #58 'support for Kinetic / Ubuntu 16.04', whose FFmpeg is 2.8). Resolved label n4.2: the calls compiled at 77a774f5 on libavcodec 58 are not deprecated in n4.2. At 77a774f5 mjpeg2rgb also no longer calls any decode function on the >52 path ("(void)MJPEG;", "(void)len;"), a behavioural change outside this case. PR #197 ('Full support for last FFMPEG', develop branch) addresses the same deprecations for the ROS 1 package: "`AVPicture` API calls are now removed in favour of correct instantiation of `AVFrame` structures." Later ros2-branch work (PR #231 refactor, PR #342 "Remove deprecared/unneeded avcodec_close()") continues the migration.
